title: The Beat of Good Prose
use_cases: Use when evaluating the density of descriptive elements in a scene
Implement when addressing issues with reader skimming or disengagement
Use when coaching writers on narrative flow versus rigid formulas
Configure when balancing atmospheric description with plot progression
content:
During a recent coaching session with a talented client working on a crime novel, we had a breakthrough moment discussing description. He asked me if there was a standard formula—”Would there be a standard like you would describe X amount of things in a room, X amount of things about a person?”

My answer surprised him: “There’s no set number that will get you to know it.”

Instead, I suggested he think about prose rhythm—the beats that carry a reader through a scene. Like music, prose has its own time signature, its own cadence and flow. When your description has the right rhythm, readers stay engaged. When it doesn’t, they skim ahead looking for the next plot point.
